en.title: Subject and verb agreement
en.summary: The verb agrees with its subject in number.

paragraphs: A verb must agree with its subject in number and person. In English this agreement is visible only in the present tense (the -s of the third person singular) and in the verb be (am, is, are, was, were) and have (has).

items: He **has** a car. / We **have** a car.

blocks.html:
SubjectRuleExample
two subjects with andpluralTom and Ann are here.
two subjects with or / noragrees with the nearerNeither he nor I am ready.
everyone, someone, nobodysingularEveryone is here.
a group noun (team, family)singular (US); singular or plural (UK)The team is / are winning.
news, mathematicssingular though they end in -sThe news is good.
scissors, trousers, glassespluralMy trousers are new.
a number of / the number ofplural / singularA number of people are here. The number is small.

paragraphs: The verb agrees with the subject, not with the noun nearest to it: The box of chocolates is on the table (not are). The key to all the doors was lost.

items: Wrong: **She work every day.** Right: **She works every day.**
Wrong: **The news are bad.** Right: **The news is bad.**
Wrong: **There is two problems.** Right: **There are two problems.**
Wrong: **Everybody are here.** Right: **Everybody is here.**
